You'll make things happen-fast.. . As a Principal Infrastructure Architect on our Infrastructure Architecture team, you will be the architecture team's partner to ZoomInfo's data engineering organization. Data engineering owns the platforms and the products built on them. You bring the infrastructure patterns, evaluation rigor, and cross-team alignment that help them build and run those platforms well on GCP. This is a cloud architect seat with a data specialty. You bring the same cloud, Kubernetes, networking, and infrastructure-as-code foundation as the rest of the architecture team, plus enough hands-on depth in data systems to be credible with the engineers who run them. The work breaks down four ways:. Patterns. You establish and maintain the paved-road patterns data teams build on: infrastructure as code, CI/CD for data jobs and pipelines, monitoring and alerting, performance, and cost. You keep them easy to consume and self-service. Enablement and alignment. You help data teams adopt those patterns, review their designs, and work through hard infrastructure trade-offs with them. Evaluation. You run POCs of new data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process, and you write recommendations engineering leaders can act on. Shared stewardship. You take a full share of the architecture team's general work: weekly architecture reviews across all domains, standards and ADRs, and infrastructure consulting for any team that needs it. The data estate is broad. We don't expect deep experience across all of it. We expect real depth in some areas and the ability to build depth in others as the work demands. Patterns get adopted here through leadership and communication rather than positional authority. You'll write reference implementations, open the first PRs, and stay hands-on through enablement when a critical initiative calls for it. What You'll Do. Establish infrastructure patterns for data workloads. Design and maintain reference patterns for provisioning and operating the data platforms ZoomInfo runs: streaming and messaging (Kafka/Confluent, Pub/Sub), operational databases (PostgreSQL/Cloud SQL, MongoDB), analytical stores (BigQuery, Snowflake), search (Elasticsearch/Solr), pipeline orchestration and processing (Apache Airflow/Cloud Composer, Dataflow/Apache Beam), and open table formats (Apache Iceberg). Ship them as Terraform modules, GitOps workflows, and documented standards that data teams can adopt without reinventing them. Build the data paved road. Today's delivery tooling is application-centric. Define CI/CD and GitOps patterns for data jobs and pipelines, and partner with platform engineering and data engineering to make data delivery as safe and automated as application delivery. Establish performance, cost, and observability patterns. Give data teams the patterns and guidance to run stores and pipelines efficiently (query and storage optimization, partitioning and clustering, tiering and retention, workload isolation, right-sizing) and the monitoring, alerting, and SLO practices that make performance and cost visible. Set the baseline patterns for backup, restore, and disaster recovery of data stores, including RTO/RPO targets. Partner with FinOps on data-layer spend. Review workloads with teams against these patterns and help them align. Evaluate new technologies. Run structured POCs of emerging data technologies and vendor offerings as part of the procurement and technology-lifecycle process. Recent examples include graph and distributed SQL databases, stream processing (Apache Flink, Confluent Flink), and schema management and cataloging. Weigh self-hosted against vendor-managed, map migration and exit paths, model cost, and write up a recommendation. Bring managed data services inside the perimeter. Define the patterns for connecting vendor-managed data planes (Confluent Cloud, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and similar) to our GCP environment: private connectivity (Private Service Connect, PrivateLink, VPC peering), VPC Service Controls, identity and encryption across the boundary (workload identity, CMEK, in-transit), and the DNS and routing that go with them. Model egress and cross-region cost, and set the exfiltration controls that keep those services inside the compliance perimeter. Support data consolidation and governance efforts. Contribute infrastructure guidance to data engineering's work on consolidating where data lives and is accessed (BigQuery, Snowflake, object storage) and on data classification, residency, and access policy. Prototype and hand off. Build the reference implementation, write the ADR, and partner with the owning teams to roll the pattern out. Stay hands-on through POC and initial enablement. Participate in architecture review. Bring a consistent, documented rubric to weekly architecture reviews across all domains, including designs that have nothing to do with data. Expand the standards library and ADR catalog. Take a share of the team's general consulting and support load. Enable teams. Host design reviews and workshops. Serve as the infrastructure consultant to data teams making complex choices. What We're Looking For. Influence and communication. You can present a recommendation, show its value, and back it with prototypes, benchmarks, and documented rationale. You've gotten patterns adopted across engineering organizations you don't manage by working with the teams involved. Cloud infrastructure foundation. Production experience architecting on GCP and/or AWS beyond the data services: compute and Kubernetes (GKE or equivalent) as the runtime for data workloads, VPC networking and private connectivity to managed services, IAM and workload identity, and cost and reliability trade-offs. Strong Terraform and GitOps skills, including designing and reviewing modules other teams depend on. You can review a service-mesh or network design in architecture review with credibility. Hands-on data infrastructure experience at scale. You've built and operated the infrastructure under data platforms at multi-terabyte to petabyte scale, with high throughput, high concurrency, and latency-sensitive workloads, and you know what breaks in production. Depth in at least two data domains, fluency across the rest. Deep production experience in at least two of: streaming and stream processing (Kafka/Confluent, Flink); relational operational databases (PostgreSQL); NoSQL (MongoDB); columnar analytics and lakehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Iceberg); search (Elasticsearch/Solr); pipeline orchestration and processing (Airflow, Dataflow/Beam). Enough fluency in the others to evaluate, review, and learn them quickly. Performance and cost engineering. You've diagnosed and fixed expensive or slow data workloads (query plans, storage layout, pipeline design, warehouse spend) and turned the fixes into reusable patterns and monitoring that other teams picked up. Development and operational depth. You can dive into code to prove out a pattern and test behavior under load, and you'd rather ship a working prototype than a diagram. Technology evaluation. You've run rigorous evaluations that separate vendor pitch from architectural fit, and your recommendations have been used by engineering leaders and procurement. Bonus Points. Supported a lakehouse or data mesh migration from the infrastructure side. Implemented data classification, residency, or privacy/compliance (GDPR/CCPA) controls at the infrastructure layer. Run graph or distributed SQL databases in production. Know the infrastructure demands of AI/ML data workloads (feature stores, vector databases, embedding pipelines). Built or applied AI-augmented developer or architecture workflows (agent-driven pipeline provisioning, MCP servers, LLM-based rubric evaluation). Run or participated in an Architecture Review Council or equivalent governance body. Education and Experience. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. 10-15+ years of cloud infrastructure, platform, or data infrastructure engineering experience, including several years establishing patterns and standards that multiple teams depend on. #LI- RA1. #LI-Remote. title: Principal Machine Learning Engineer
description: ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute. You'll make things happen-fast.. You'll set the technical direction for the intelligence layer every ZoomInfo AI agent reasons over - what's true about companies and the people in them, how they relate, and what they're buying. As a senior individual contributor with no direct reports, you will own strategy across the data graph, entity resolution, and buying intent, staying hands-on in the hardest of these problems. You'll decide when classical machine learning, statistics, or language models is the right tool, and turn good judgment into standards other teams adopt. What You'll Do. You will set technical strategy for the data graph, entity resolution, buying intent, and agent context, deciding which problems to take on, in what order, and how the pieces connect. You will frame and ship problems nobody has framed yet, such as extraction for companies with no public footprint or semantic intent at web scale, deciding what not to build as deliberately as what to build. You will define evaluation standards that other teams adopt, including sampling methodology, human labels, validated LLM judges, and release gates, and know where each one breaks. You will define the data contracts between the data graph, intent signals, and the agents that consume them, including agent memory, keeping the system cost-effective to run across the full dataset. You will turn good choices into defaults across the group: the baseline every model must beat, how uncertainty is reported, and which metrics get retired when they mislead. You will lead design reviews, mentor senior engineers, shape hiring, and represent the team's technical judgment to product and leadership. What You Bring. Must-Have:. You have set technical direction as an individual contributor for a problem area spanning more than one team, with the resulting machine learning systems in production and owned after launch - depth of impact matters more than years or past titles. You bring breadth across classical machine learning on large, messy tabular data, applied statistics, language processing at scale, and LLM agents or multi-step systems, with recognized depth in at least one. You have defined and driven adoption of evaluation standards beyond your own team for systems with no single right answer, including LLM judges validated against human labels and results reported with their limits. You have a track record of changing how a group builds or measures - for example, introducing a baseline or review practice that other teams now use. You have made cost and capacity decisions for model training and serving, including when to self-host, distill, or call a hosted model, with cost tracked per unit of work. You are hands-on in production Python and strong SQL with distributed data processing experience, and you use AI coding tools daily with rigorous review of their output. Preferred:. You have experience with ranking and retrieval, including embeddings, learned re-ranking, and metrics such as recall@k, MRR, and nDCG. You bring entity resolution, knowledge graph, or web-scale information extraction experience on messy, real-world data. You have trained and served open-weight models in PyTorch or an equivalent framework, including GPU capacity planning. You have built user memory or context systems for agents, or defended LLM systems against adversarial inputs and prompt injection.. . #LI-Remote. #LI-VC1. title: Principal Product Designer, Agentic Chat
description: ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute. You'll make things happen-fast.. Principal Product Designer, Agentic Chat. You'll lead the design of how people experience agents inside GTM One, ZoomInfo's unified go-to-market platform for sellers, marketers, and revenue teams. In agentic chat, the agent's behavior is the experience, and you own that experience end to end: how it acts, how it asks, what it costs, and how it proves itself before a customer finds out otherwise. This is a Principal seat defined by surface ownership, not feature delivery - you'll set direction for agent experience across every way a customer reaches an agent, and you'll be expected to bring proposals forward rather than wait for a brief. You will:. • Own the agent experience across universal chat, including how the agent communicates status, asks for input, and reports back on long-running work. • Design the interactions that let agents create artifacts, apps, and automations built on context, and define how those outputs show up to the customer. • Build cost estimation and credit-approval moments into chat, so customers understand what an agent action costs before and after it runs. • Establish evals as a design instrument, using evaluation results to prove an experience is ready before launch and to guide what changes after real users touch it. • Design the trust mechanics that let customers calibrate confidence in agent output, including how failure, uncertainty, and partial results are shown. • Prototype in code, open pull requests, and ship working proposals directly into the codebase alongside engineering. • Partner with product management and engineering on orchestration and tool infrastructure while owning what the customer actually experiences of it. • Define problems alongside solutions, operating with thin briefs and acting as a product thinker on your surface area. What You Bring. Must-Have:. • At least 2 years designing AI or agentic products where the model's behavior was the product itself (not AI features layered onto a conventional surface), and you can speak candidly to what went wrong in front of real users. • Experience running evals: you have built or used an evaluation setup for an agent, and you can explain how you knew it was ready before launch and what changed after real users touched it. • A track record of shipping in code: you prototype with AI coding tools (not only in Figma), you open pull requests, and you can read a backend contract, even if you are not an engineer by title. • A working understanding of how LLMs behave in production, including latency, streaming, tool calling, confidence, and failure modes, and you design for those honestly rather than defaulting to the happy path. • Experience working directly with engineering in their channels and on their timelines, as a core part of how you ship. Preferred:. • Domain depth designing for sellers, marketers, RevOps, or CS inside a CRM, sales-engagement, data, or revenue-intelligence product. • Experience with enterprise complexity, data-dense interfaces, bulk operations, or long-running jobs without losing clarity for the end user. • Experience designing for a product where usage directly costs the customer money. • Comfort blending UX research with agentic design - using research to predict and evals to confirm. How We Evaluate. You'll be assessed across four axes, shared with you in advance: context engineering and agentic systems (including eval experience); the blend of UX research and agentic design; aesthetic quality and experience craft; and engineering fundamentals. No one is expected to score highest on all four - we want to know where you'd place yourself so we know how to work together. Interviews include walking through a real agent-surface decision (including an argument you lost), an eval you ran and what it changed, a live conversation about a go-to-market workflow, a working session on an open problem, and a look at your own tooling. No spec work, no unpaid take-home, and no design challenge we'd actually ship. #LI-Remote. #LI-ST2. title: Principal Product Management, Growth
description: ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute. You'll make things happen-fast.. Principal Product Manager, Growth. About ZoomInfo. ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute - you'll make things happen, fast. The Opportunity. Own a Growth Portfolio and Set the Pattern the Rest of the Team Inherits. ZoomInfo built the industry's most sophisticated GTM data platform. The next frontier is turning every visitor into revenue without waiting on a human handoff - a coherent self-serve journey that activates a non-customer in minutes, converts consumption into upgrade, and routes high-intent signals back to sales when a human will close more than they distract. You'll define the multi-quarter thesis on which channels compound, the operating rhythm the rest of the growth PM team inherits, and the ZoomInfo POV on how buyers discover us in an AI-first world. The impact is immediate and compounding. Every signup you activate, every credit you cause to be consumed, every transaction, every PQL you route, every "buy more" event you trigger is revenue - and every operating pattern you set multiplies across the growth PM group. We've adopted a consumption-first monetization model and a unified entry-point thesis across the company, and we run weekly: if your hypothesis can't be falsified inside a sprint, it isn't a hypothesis. This is a rare opportunity to own a P&L-shaped surface with full air cover to ship fast, learn in public, re-pivot when the data turns - and to define the growth PM craft as ZoomInfo scales it. What You'll Do. Own the Portfolio End-to-End. Take a portfolio-scope growth surface - and own it from first impression to revenue. Define the entry points, the activation milestones, the monetization moments, and the sales-assist signals across the channels that make up the portfolio. Drive the user experience across surfaces: landing, signup, in-product onboarding, empty states, upgrade modals, paywalls, lifecycle communication, and the agent-readable / LLM-discovery surfaces that are becoming primary. You own the funnel chart; you own the why behind every drop. Set the Multi-Quarter Growth Thesis. Beyond weekly experiments, own 4-8 quarter bets on which channels compound and which retire. Publish a written POV on where PLG distribution is heading (LLM-first discovery, MCP-as-channel, agent-readable onboarding, partner-driven trials) and defend the sequencing to the exec team. Rebalance investment across the portfolio quarterly based on unit economics, not the loudest channel. Run Experimentation as the Operating Rhythm - and Set the Rhythm for the Team. Ship 8-10 experiments per sprint. Pre-register the hypothesis, the metric, the success threshold, and - critically - the invalidation signal. Read results weekly, kill what doesn't work, double down on what does, and keep a written record so the team compounds learning instead of repeating it. Your rubric, your retro format, and your invalidation-signal standard become the template the rest of the Growth PM group inherits. Translate results into concrete changes: copy rewrites, schema tweaks, pricing changes, new flows, retired ones. Close the loop with engineering, design, and analytics inside the same week. Design Self-Serve as a First-Class Path. Most users on your portfolio never speak to sales before they hit a "buy more" moment. Your in-product copy, paywall framing, empty states, activation paths, and upgrade triggers are the product. Apply growth-engineering rigor - credit economics, consumption pacing, signal routing, lifecycle messaging, intelligent gating - so the right offer lands in front of the right user at exactly the right moment. Hand high-intent users to sales with a clean signal; absorb low-intent users with a clean self-serve path. Diagnose the Funnel With Data, Not Vibes. Data is your default tool, not a thing you ask analytics to do for you. You independently analyze the funnel, segment the cohort, find the leak, and propose the fix - then validate it with an experiment. You know when to trust a 5% lift and when to call it noise. Just as important: you know when to zoom out from a specific funnel drop to a portfolio-level rebalance, and can defend that call. Shape the Monetization Mechanic. You'll design the credit economics of your portfolio: what's free, what's gated, what gets a "buy more" prompt, what triggers a PQL. You'll model the unit economics - credit cost, revenue per credit, upgrade rate, expansion rate - and you'll defend the pricing decisions in front of finance and sales leadership with the math. Orchestrate Across Sales, Marketing, and CS. Self-serve doesn't mean alone. You'll route PQLs into the right hands (AE, SC, AM, or no one), partner with marketing on acquisition and lifecycle, and work with CS to understand why activated users churn before upgrade. You'll run the operating cadences that keep your portfolio aligned with the broader PLG portfolio without becoming a meeting machine. Multiply the Team. Help hire and calibrate the Sr Growth PMs owning adjacent loops. Coach them into ownership. Your retro is their template; your experiment quality is their bar. Raise the craft of the whole Growth PM group as it scales. Stay Honest About What's Working. Write retrospectives that name the wrong calls as cleanly as the right ones. Update your priors publicly when the data turns. Hold strong opinions weakly. The team that ships the most experiments isn't the team that's right the most - it's the team that updates the fastest. What You'll Bring. 8-12 years of product management experience, with 4+ years specifically in growth, PLG, or self-serve product roles. Direct P&L ownership at portfolio scope - a loop or portfolio you've driven from <$X to >$Y with your name on the number, not a feature inside someone else's loop. Experience presenting to CEO / CRO / CFO / board on growth mechanics - the credit-economics deck, the funnel narrative, the "kill this bet" moment. Track record of hiring, mentoring, or calibrating other growth PMs - comfortable being the bar. You're a builder. You ship landing pages, signup flows, and in-product experiments - not specs that sit in Jira. You sit with designers and engineers, write copy, and prototype with code. AI-fluent with a public POV. You understand that LLMs are becoming a primary discovery surface. You have opinions - publishable ones - about agent-readable flows, MCP-as-distribution, GEO/AEO, and how an AI agent's recommendation impacts a funnel. Marketing-fluent. You hold your own with SEO, paid acquisition, content, and lifecycle marketing teams as a peer, not a consumer. Demonstrated track record of running structured experimentation (A/B tests, multivariate, holdouts, pre/post) at sprint cadence - including at cohort sizes where 50/50 doesn't have power. Strong analytics fluency - comfortable in Snowflake without analyst hand-holding. Working knowledge of consumption-based pricing, credit economics, freemium mechanics, and PQL frameworks. B2B SaaS background; data, GTM, or sales-tech domain experience is a plus but not required. Who You Are. Core Competencies. Funnel Foundation. Expert-level understanding of full-funnel growth. You can reason about activation rates, time-to-value, retention curves, credit economics, upgrade triggers, and PQL signal quality with depth. You've owned a growth loop - or portfolio - in production. SQL and analytics fluency let you diagnose a funnel drop, prototype the fix, and validate it in the same week. Portfolio Thinking. You reason about ToF (or an equivalent surface) as a portfolio of channels with different unit economics, decay curves, and compounding dynamics - not a single funnel. You rebalance investment quarterly based on where marginal dollars return the most, and you can defend the rebalance to leadership with the math. Experimentation Discipline. You don't ship without a hypothesis. You pre-register the metric and the invalidation signal before the test runs. You read results honestly, kill losing variants without ego, and document learnings so the team compounds knowledge instead of relitigating settled questions. You know the difference between an experiment and a launch - and you can tell when each is the right move. Category POV. You have a public, defensible point of view on where PLG distribution is heading - agent-readable surfaces, MCP-as-channel, GEO/AEO, LLM-first onboarding - grounded in benchmarks from peer companies (Clay, Linear, Vercel, Cursor, Notion), not just internal data. That POV shows up in the roadmap. Distribution Mindset. Experience designing growth surfaces where sales teams, marketing teams, and self-serve users are simultaneously your customers. You measure success through revenue, consumption, and expansion velocity, not screens shipped. You understand growth economics: each additional entry point, freemium offer, or AI trial compounds in value through shared activation patterns, amortized acquisition costs, and recurring consumption network effects. Operational Velocity. You read the funnel daily, not quarterly. You prototype emerging mechanics - paywalls, in-app prompts, lifecycle sequences - to understand their practical constraints before committing engineering time. You hold strong opinions weakly, updating your design assumptions as evidence accumulates, publicly, even when the prior thesis was your own. Strategic Communication. You translate between funnel depth and business impact fluently. You can explain to the CEO why a credit pricing change is worth a quarter of work. You can communicate to engineers why a revenue constraint requires a "quiet release" in two weeks rather than a polished launch in three months. You influence without formal authority through forcing functions, falsifiable invalidation signals, and earned credibility. Talent Leverage. You coach Sr PMs into full ownership of their loops. Your retro is their template. Your experiment quality is their bar. You help hire the next PMs on the team, and you calibrate - you know what "great" looks like at Sr level and you can articulate the gap to someone who isn't there yet. Copy Instinct. Microcopy is part of your craft, not someone else's job. You can rewrite a paywall headline, an upgrade modal, an empty state, or an onboarding CTA on instinct - and defend the rewrite with PLG principles. You know when to ask content design for help and when to ship the rewrite yourself. The Environment. Reporting, Pace & Impact. Reporting & Collaboration. Report to the VP Product, PLG. Peer to the Sr Directors of Marketing, Sales Operations, and Customer Success on the growth contracts (PQL routing, demand-gen alignment, credit economics). Work shoulder-to-shoulder with the engineering and design leaders building the underlying surfaces, the GTM leaders routing PQLs into sales, and a peer PM group covering monetization, lifecycle, viral, onboarding, and analytics. Regular exposure to the CEO, CRO, CMO, and CFO - you own those conversations at your level. Pace & Problems. Fast-moving teams that understand the space. Weekly experimentation cadence layered under 4-quarter portfolio bets. Expect interesting problems: How do we win activation in a user's first 60 seconds? When should two trial flows become one? How do we expose enough value to convert without giving away the platform? How do we price a credit so that customers consume more, not less? When should a self-serve user be routed to sales - and when does that routing actually destroy revenue? How do buyers discover ZoomInfo when discovery goes through Claude and ChatGPT? Your decisions become operating patterns across the PLG organization. Impact. Own a portfolio-scope growth surface at a company that is already AI-first in product thinking and consumption-first in monetization. Your decisions compound. Every improvement to the funnel, the offer, or the activation experience multiplies across multiple products, every partner-driven self-serve channel ZoomInfo ships into, and every AI distribution surface we haven't yet imagined - and every operating pattern you set makes the next PM on the team better. What changed at a glance:. Title + opening reframed from loop-scope → portfolio-scope, ToF-leaning but flexible. Three new sections in What You'll Do: Set the Multi-Quarter Thesis, Represent PLG to Leadership, Multiply the Team. Seniority bar: 4-7 yrs → 8-12 yrs; adds direct P&L ownership, exec/board presenting, hiring/mentoring. Two new competencies: Portfolio Thinking, Category POV, Talent Leverage. Reporting line: Sr Director → VP Product, PLG; peer to CRO/CMO/CFO direct reports. We're investing in the team behind it. We're hiring a Principal Product Manager to own datasets end to end: where the data comes from, how it's built and resolved to ZoomInfo's company and contact universe, how it shows up across every surface we sell through, how it's priced and packaged, and how much revenue it generates. You'll also be the internal subject matter expert on these datasets: the data itself, the sources, the competitive landscape, and how customers actually use it. We spend a lot of our time close to our strategic customers, working strategic opportunities directly with customers and our sales teams, shaping deals, and figuring out what a dataset needs to look like for a customer to actually buy it. Increasingly that means thinking in solutions, not single datasets. Source the data (public records, partner licensing, our own extraction and classification). Decide what "done" looks like for a dataset and hold the line on it. Platform delivery. Partner with data engineering and platform engineering to get datasets out of the warehouse, into the GTM Data Store, and live across every surface: our APIs, MCP, and our applications. Write the requirements, define the use case queries, own the testing, drive the handoffs. This is the stage where most data products die. You'll make sure ours don't. Commercialization. title: Senior Forward Deployed Engineer
description: ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You'll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won't just contribute. You'll make things happen-fast.. The Role. ZoomInfo is building its Forward Deployed Engineering function. You will help define how it operates - how engagements run, what the deliverables are, how the playbook works, what scales and what doesn't. The support structure exists (data team, product team, infrastructure, executive sponsorship); what's needed is someone who brings it to life in front of customers and helps turn early wins into a repeatable model. As an FDE, you embed directly with ZoomInfo's strategic accounts - large enterprises with complex data needs, often in financial services, insurance, technology, and other globally distributed industries. You work alongside their teams to understand their go-to-market challenges, then help design and deliver bespoke intelligence applications that combine ZoomInfo's third-party data with the customer's first-party data to drive real business outcomes. You own your engagements end-to-end: from discovery through deployment, from stakeholder presentations through production code. You'll work closely with our data and product teams (and alongside more senior FDEs on larger accounts) to bring the full breadth of ZoomInfo's data foundation to bear - company intelligence, contact data, buying signals, intent data, and specialized vertical datasets - assembled into purpose-built applications tailored to each customer's specific personas and workflows. ZoomInfo has one of the deepest go-to-market data foundations in the world - 500M+ professional profiles, 100M+ company records, intent signals, vertical datasets spanning financial filings, insurance, commercial fleet, and more. You'll have access to incredible data, powerful infrastructure, and exposure to our most important customer relationships. What you build with them - and how you build it - will help define the model going forward. What Engagements Typically Look Like. A few recurring patterns show up across strategic accounts. Most engagements involve some combination of:. Entity resolution at scale - reconciling legal entity hierarchies (D&B, tax IDs, company-house registrations) with how customers actually go to market. Multinationals with hundreds of legal entities collapsing to a single GTM record. Hierarchy management - enforcing one-to-one matching across regions, fixing parent-child linkage gaps, dispositioning orphaned accounts, surfacing white space on top of clean parent IDs. Location-level precision - moving customers off monolithic HQ-level enrichment so geo-based sales teams see local firmographics instead of global rollups. Automated, no-human-in-the-loop logic - entity suppression, disposition-based matching, orchestration rules for inactive entities, parent linkages, and white space alerts. Data warehouse as the operating layer - moving sophisticated analysis out of CRM (Salesforce can't do hierarchy work at scale) into Snowflake or BigQuery, via API or data cube depending on the workflow. Buying group filtering - applying persona-density criteria across hierarchies to turn a customer's 5,600 Disney legal entities into 31 actionable targets. Two recent engagements as concrete reference points:. A global infrastructure customer brought us 1.8M records and 300K flagged as "unmatched," with a data team of one. An automated domain validation pipeline reframed the problem entirely - 175K inactive sites, 30K redirects, 65K real opportunities - and turned a "coverage gap" conversation into a data quality program. An enterprise planning platform had 120K Salesforce accounts, broken hierarchies, and field leaders reporting near-zero confidence in their enrichment data. The underlying data was accurate; the matching was wrong. Custom disposition logic on a 10K-account priority sample produced 7,444 high-confidence matches at 98-99% accuracy - validated before scaling the framework to the full universe. This is the work. It moves between data engineering, applied product development, and stakeholder management - often in the same week. What You'll Build. Every engagement comprises a consistent service architecture - three pillars built on top of each other, and five capability areas assembled into the actual deliverable. Three pillars:. Data Foundation - golden reference matching, persistent IDs, unified entity profiles across the customer's first-party systems. Data Management - business-specific logic that turns the foundation into something the customer can actually go to market with: customer definitions, account models, entity resolution. Activation - TAM to SAM to SOM, fit scoring, in-market signals. Five capability areas:. Data Foundation Development - Match every record across the customer's CRM, ERP, billing, and marketing systems to a golden reference dataset. Build custom disposition logic, domain validation, marketability classification, and legal entity crosswalks. The output is a single persistent ID linking every system. Account Architecture & Entity Resolution - Define what an account means for the customer's business (address-based, country, HQ, ultimate-parent rollup, or hybrid), then build automated logic that enforces that structure: duplicate resolution, inactive entity disposition, hierarchy linkages. TAM Development & White Space Discovery - Build the customer's complete addressable market against ICP criteria, suppress against existing customers via ultimate-parent rollup, surface white space inside customer hierarchies, and apply buying group filters to reduce overwhelming entity volume to targeted pipeline. Account Fit Scoring & In-Market Signals - Build custom fit models from historical win/loss patterns; configure both evergreen signals (executive moves, leadership changes, funding rounds) and tailored ones (intent topic spikes, senior job postings, technology displacement events). Ongoing Governance & Automation - Match orchestration rules, enrichment segmentation, CRM field locking, and warehouse integration (Snowflake, BigQuery) that keep the foundation clean as the business evolves. Most engagements use at least three of these. You'll work with your manager and more senior FDEs to diagnose which the customer actually needs, scope the work, and deliver - taking on increasing ownership of that diagnosis as you build track record. What You'll Do. Own Strategic Customer Engagements End-to-End Serve as a primary technical point of contact for assigned strategic accounts. Run discovery sessions with data engineers, sales operations leaders, and revenue stakeholders. Help diagnose the underlying problem (which is rarely the one the customer first describes - "we have a coverage gap" often turns out to be a marketability problem, "we don't trust the data" often turns out to be a matching problem). Scope the use case, design the solution, build the application, deploy it in the customer's environment, and stay accountable for the outcome - not just the delivery. Bridge Technical and Business Audiences Sit with the sales team. Present to customer stakeholders. Synthesize complex go-to-market data needs into clear, actionable proposals - then deliver the solution. You're comfortable whiteboarding matching architecture with a data engineering team and walking a sales operations director through disposition codes, and you're developing the ability to present ROI and strategy to executive audiences. Contribute to the FDE Playbook Document what works: discovery frameworks, engagement phases, integration patterns, deliverable templates, success metrics. The current strategic-account engagements are reference patterns - help extract what's repeatable from each new account and feed it into a model that scales to additional strategic accounts, verticals, and eventually a larger team. Feed field learnings back to product, engineering, and data teams to inform product direction and dataset priorities. Drive Stickiness and Expansion Every application you build embeds ZoomInfo more deeply into the customer's daily workflows. Help identify expansion opportunities as they emerge - new use cases, new personas, new datasets, displacement opportunities against incumbent providers. What We're Looking For. High Ownership, Comfort with Ambiguity This function is still being defined at ZoomInfo. You take ownership of your workstreams, are comfortable making judgment calls with incomplete information, and can operate effectively even where process doesn't yet exist. Strong Software and Data Engineering Fundamentals You write production-quality code. You're proficient in Python and SQL, and comfortable working in cloud data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks, or similar). You've built or substantially worked with: data pipelines, entity matching or deduplication logic, API integrations, and applications that real users depend on daily. Familiarity with API tooling - GraphQL, REST, Postman, authentication patterns (JWT, OAuth) - is a plus; deep expertise isn't required, but you should be comfortable navigating and integrating against APIs quickly. You work fluently in LLM-based development environments like Claude Code or Codex - these are core tools in how we build, not a nice-to-have. Customer-Facing Communication You've worked directly with customers in a technical capacity - solutions engineering, consulting, technical account management, or a previous FDE-style role. You can synthesize complex data needs for a business audience and discuss matching architecture with a data engineering team in the same week, if not the same meeting. You're comfortable navigating enterprise environments with competing stakeholders - sales operations, IT, marketing ops, finance, and revenue leadership all sit at the same table. Go-to-Market Data Familiarity (Preferred) Experience working with B2B data, CRM systems (Salesforce, HubSpot), enrichment and orchestration tooling (RingLead, Clearbit, Demandbase), or similar go-to-market infrastructure. Familiarity with concepts like firmographic enrichment, entity resolution, hierarchy management, TAM modeling, intent data, and account-based prospecting. This isn't required - if you're a fast learner with the right instincts, we'll get you there. Why This Role The mandate is clear. Driving data consumption and growth across ZoomInfo's strategic accounts is a top company priority. We already have working prototypes, validated customer demand, and executive sponsorship. The data team, product team, and infrastructure are in place. What's needed is someone ready to execute and grow with the function. Enterprise customer access. ZoomInfo's customer base includes market-leading GTM organizations at some of the largest enterprises in the world. You'll be embedded with these teams, solving real problems with meaningful budgets and complex data needs. Best-in-class data and infrastructure. ZoomInfo's data foundation, GTM Data Store, query infrastructure, and vertical dataset catalog give you the raw materials to build custom intelligence applications that aren't possible anywhere else. #LI-AR2 #LI-remote. Proven reliability: We always ground our innovation in our deep experience and strong financial foundation, so we're a partner you can trust.. What You'll Do:. . Customers Bank is seeking an experienced Real Estate Specialty Finance - Senior Analyst / Portfolio Manager to support the growth and ongoing management of the Bank's national Real Estate Specialty Finance Lending platform.. This position will be responsible for underwriting new note-on-note lending opportunities, analyzing the underlying commercial real estate loan collateral, assisting with transaction structuring and closing, and providing ongoing administration and monitoring of existing note-on-note facilities.. The successful candidate will have a strong commercial real estate credit background and the ability to analyze both the underlying commercial real estate loans and the financial strength, experience, and performance of the lending platform serving as Customers Bank's borrower.. The role will work closely with the Head of Specialty Lending, Relationship Managers, CRE Credit, Loan Administration, Legal, and other internal partners throughout the entire transaction lifecycle-from initial underwriting and approval through closing, funding, ongoing collateral administration, and portfolio monitoring.. Credit Underwriting & Analysis. Underwrite new commercial real estate note-on-note and lender finance transactions in accordance with Customers Bank's credit policies and risk standards. Perform detailed analysis of the underlying commercial real estate loans securing each facility. Review and analyze property-level operating performance, rent rolls, borrower financial statements, appraisals, market information, and other relevant due diligence. Evaluate key CRE credit metrics, including LTV/LTC, debt yield, DSCR, occupancy, cash flow, sponsorship, liquidity, loan maturity, and exit strategy. Analyze the structure and terms of the underlying CRE loans, including interest rates, maturity dates, extension options, reserves, cash management provisions, guarantees, and other structural protections. Evaluate the experience, financial strength, capitalization, liquidity, track record, and lending strategy of the note-on-note borrower. Review borrower portfolio performance, historical losses, delinquencies, modifications, defaults, and realized loan performance, where applicable. Identify key transaction risks and recommend appropriate structural mitigants. Assist in establishing advance rates, borrowing base requirements, concentration limits, eligibility criteria, covenants, reserves, and other facility-level protections. Prepare comprehensive credit approval memoranda and supporting financial analysis. Present underwriting conclusions and respond to questions from Relationship Managers, senior management, and credit approval authorities. Assist with annual reviews, renewals, modifications, extensions, and increases to existing credit facilities.. Note-on-Note Facility Administration. Provide ongoing administration and monitoring of the Bank's Real Estate Specialty Finance lending facilities. Review borrower funding and advance requests and confirm compliance with approved advance rates and facility requirements. Review and validate borrowing base certificates and supporting collateral schedules. Confirm that loans submitted for funding satisfy established collateral eligibility requirements. Calculate or verify availability under borrowing base facilities prior to funding. Maintain detailed collateral tracking for each note-on-note facility. Monitor underlying loan balances, paydowns, repayments, maturities, extensions, modifications, and other material changes. Track facility-level and loan-level concentration limits, including property type, geography, borrower/sponsor, loan size, leverage, and other applicable limitations. Monitor required collateral documentation and ensure appropriate assignments, control agreements, original loan documents, and other required items are received and maintained. Coordinate with Loan Administration and Operations regarding advances, paydowns, interest payments, principal payments, and other facility activity. Review collateral releases and payoffs and confirm compliance with applicable loan documentation. Maintain accurate internal records and reporting for all assigned facilities.. Portfolio Monitoring & Risk Management. Monitor the ongoing credit performance of both the note-on-note borrower and the underlying commercial real estate collateral. Review periodic borrower financial statements, compliance certificates, borrowing base reports, collateral reports, and other required reporting. Monitor underlying loans for changes in occupancy, cash flow, DSCR, debt yield, valuation, sponsorship, maturity, and business plan execution. Identify and escalate deteriorating credit trends, covenant violations, collateral deficiencies, documentation exceptions, and other emerging risks. Monitor watchlist loans and other criticized or higher-risk underlying collateral. Assist with internal risk ratings and changes to risk ratings as appropriate. Prepare periodic portfolio reports summarizing facility utilization, collateral composition, concentrations, upcoming maturities, credit trends, and identified risks. Assist with stress testing and portfolio-level analysis as required. Support internal and external audits, regulatory examinations, loan reviews, and other portfolio reviews. Ensure assigned facilities remain in compliance with approved credit terms, Bank policies, and applicable regulatory requirements.. Transaction Closing & Documentation. Work closely with Relationship Managers, Credit, Legal, Loan Administration, and outside counsel throughout the closing process. Review approved credit terms against final loan documentation to ensure consistency with credit approval. Assist with review of loan agreements, borrowing base provisions, collateral assignments, control agreements, guarantees, and other transaction documents. Track closing conditions and outstanding documentation requirements. Coordinate receipt and review of required third-party reports and due diligence. Ensure all required credit and collateral documentation is received prior to funding or appropriately documented as an approved exception. Assist with post-closing documentation and exception tracking.. Relationship & Internal Support. Work closely with the Relationship Managers to evaluate new opportunities and efficiently move transactions through the underwriting and approval process. Participate in calls and meetings with existing and prospective borrowers as appropriate. Develop an understanding of each client's lending strategy, underwriting standards, portfolio composition, funding requirements, and business plan. Provide credit and portfolio insights to Relationship Managers to assist with structuring new transactions and expanding existing relationships. Serve as a key liaison among Relationship Management, Credit, Loan Administration, Legal, Operations, and other internal stakeholders. Support the continued development of processes, procedures, reporting, and controls for Customers Bank's national Note-on-Note Lending platform.. Role Objective. . . The primary objective of the Real Estate Specialty Finance - Senior Analyst / Portfolio Manager is to provide the credit underwriting, transaction execution, collateral administration, and ongoing portfolio monitoring necessary to support the safe and efficient growth of Customers Bank's national Note-on-Note Lending platform. The individual will play an important role in maintaining strong credit quality while helping the Bank provide responsive and efficient execution for its institutional commercial real estate lending clients.. What Do You Need?. Bachelor's degree in Finance, Real Estate, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field. Minimum of 2-5 years of commercial real estate underwriting, credit analysis, portfolio management, or loan administration experience. Strong commercial real estate underwriting and financial analysis skills. Experience with note-on-note lending, loan-on-loan financing, lender finance, warehouse lending, debt funds, private credit, or commercial real estate bridge lending preferred. Strong understanding of CRE credit metrics, including LTV, LTC, DSCR, debt yield, occupancy, cash flow, and sponsor financial analysis. Experience underwriting multiple commercial real estate property types, including multifamily, industrial, retail, office, hospitality, and other CRE assets. Ability to understand and analyze complex commercial real estate loan structures. Familiarity with borrowing base facilities, advance rates, eligibility criteria, concentration limits, and collateral administration preferred. Experience reviewing commercial real estate loan documentation and third-party reports. Strong financial modeling and Microsoft Excel skills. Strong written credit analysis and communication skills. Highly organized and detail-oriented with the ability to manage multiple transactions and deadlines simultaneously. Ability to identify credit and operational issues and escalate matters appropriately. Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with Relationship Management, Credit, Legal, Loan Administration, and Operations.. Key Attributes for Success. Strong CRE Credit Foundation - Demonstrates sound commercial real estate underwriting skills and credit judgment. Detail Oriented - Maintains accurate collateral, borrowing base, covenant, and facility-level information. Analytical - Able to evaluate both individual underlying loans and overall portfolio-level risk. Risk Focused - Proactively identifies emerging credit issues and understands their potential impact on the Bank's position. Execution Oriented - Effectively manages underwriting, closing, funding, and ongoing administrative responsibilities. Organized - Able to manage multiple facilities, funding requests, deadlines, and reporting requirements. Collaborative - Works effectively across Relationship Management, Credit, Legal, Loan Administration, Operations, and other areas of the Bank. Growth Mindset - Interested in helping develop the infrastructure, processes, and controls necessary to support the continued expansion of a national note-on-note lending platform.. Technology Skills:. Strong financial modeling and Microsoft Excel skills, with the ability to work with the Microsoft Suite and other Customers Bank applications. Familiarity with AI and automation tools that support productivity, workflow efficiency, and client engagement.. . Customers Bank is an equal opportunity employer. title: Director, Corporate Communications
description: Director, Corporate Communications. Work location. Toronto, Ontario (hybrid). About us. At NATIONAL, we are driven by purpose, creativity, and connection. For 50 years, our teams across Canada have helped organizations navigate change, build trust, and shape conversations that matter. As one of Canada's largest independent communications consultancies, we partner with leading public and private organizations to solve complex business challenges through strategic communications, corporate affairs, capital markets expertise, and creative thinking. Our Toronto team is looking for a senior communications leader with a strong background in financial communications, capital markets, and investor relations. This role is a good fit for someone who enjoys advising senior clients, making complicated business issues easier to understand, and working in a collaborative, fast-paced consulting environment. If you are a trusted advisor who likes solving complex challenges, building lasting client relationships, and helping grow a dynamic practice, we would like to hear from you. The role. This is a hands-on senior advisory opportunity for someone who wants to be both strategic and practical, commercially minded and collaborative, and comfortable advising clients when the stakes are high. As Director, Corporate Communications, you will provide senior strategic counsel to executives, boards of directors, and investor relations teams. You will lead complex client mandates across corporate and financial communications, investor relations, capital markets initiatives, reputation management, crisis files, transaction communications, disclosure support, and special situations. You will also play an important role in growing our practice. That means identifying and leading new business opportunities, expanding existing client relationships, mentoring colleagues, and connecting clients with the right expertise from across NATIONAL's practices and offices. What you will do. As a senior member of the Toronto team, you will help clients communicate clearly in moments that matter to their business, their investors, their employees, their regulators, and other important stakeholders. You will be expected to bring sound judgment, strong business instincts, and a clear understanding of how markets, media, investors, disclosure, and reputation intersect. You will lead complex client mandates from planning through execution, making sure the work is thoughtful, high quality, delivered on time, and managed on budget. You will build strong, enduring client relationships, identify opportunities to expand existing mandates, and lead new business opportunities that contribute to the growth of the Firm. You will also manage project planning, financial management, and resource allocation so that client objectives are met and the work runs smoothly. You will collaborate with colleagues across NATIONAL's practices and offices to deliver integrated communications solutions that meet evolving client needs. You will mentor, coach, and develop team members, helping foster a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing culture. You will stay close to capital markets trends, regulatory developments, and emerging communications practices so that your counsel is current, practical, and grounded in the realities of the market. You will also help strengthen NATIONAL's presence in the Canadian capital markets and financial communications community. What you bring. You are a trusted advisor with a strong grounding in financial communications. You understand how to translate complex financial, market, and business issues into clear advice, credible messaging, and practical communications plans. You are comfortable in senior rooms, including engaging with executives, boards, investor relations teams, legal advisors, bankers, analysts, and other stakeholders who are often part of high-profile, sensitive, or crisis-related mandates. You do not need to be a specialist in every situation, but you should bring the judgment and experience to know what matters, what questions to ask, and how to bring the right people together. You likely bring:. 10+ years of experience in financial and corporate communications, capital markets, investor relations, strategic communications, or a consulting or corporate advisory environment. Demonstrated experience providing strategic counsel to senior executives and leading complex communications or capital markets mandates, including crisis files. Exceptional writing, presentation, and strategic communications skills, with the ability to develop compelling messaging across multiple channels. Proven experience leading client relationships, managing budgets, and delivering complex projects in a fast-paced consulting environment. A strong understanding of capital markets, financial communications, and the evolving media and digital landscape. A bachelor's degree in Communications, Business, Finance, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related discipline. Experience advising publicly traded companies, investor relations teams or capital market participants is considered an asset. Familiarity with the Canadian capital markets landscape is also an asset. Comfort using AI-enabled tools, for example, ChatGPT. Nice to have: bilingualism in English and French. How you work. You are strategic, but not removed from the work. You can see the larger picture, identify what matters, and turn advice into action. You are calm under pressure, clear in your counsel, and comfortable working in situations where the path forward is not always obvious. You simplify complex issues, including financial and capital markets issues, and provide practical recommendations that clients can use. You bring a strong client-service mindset, build relationships naturally, and know how to manage stakeholders with confidence and discretion. Coinbase Tokenized Equities give eligible non-US users a simple way to buy tokens backed 1:1 by US stocks and ETFs - no brokerage account needed. The tokens are issued out of Abu Dhabi Global Market (ADGM), a regulated financial center overseen by the FSRA, and trade 24/7 onchain. We're hiring an Accounting Manager to be the finance lead for this product. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who likes to build. You'll own the accounting and reporting model from the ground up - accounting policy, regulatory and legal entity reporting, controls, GL operations, and finance systems - coordinating across Tax, Treasury, FP&A, and controllership, as well as external auditors and regulators. If you like solving hard problems and building from scratch, this role is for you. What You'll Do. Build the accounting model from the ground up - covering token issuance and redemption, asset tracking, intercompany flows, and the close process. Own regulatory compliance and reporting to the FSRA for this business. This includes liaising with the regulator to ensure a consistent understand of the rules, building a robust, efficient and well controlled reporting process and remaining responsive ad hoc queries. Partner with Product, Engineering, Legal, Tax, Compliance, Treasury, FP&A, and Finance Data so new flows are accurate, controlled, and scalable. Sign off on flow of funds, posting rules, account setup, ledger structure, reconciliations, and reporting before launch. Lead accounting analysis for new structures under US GAAP and IFRS, including dividends, splits, and balance sheet treatment. Build the reporting framework for our issuer entity, including annual audited IFRS financials, local filings, and external audit support. Set up a control environment for a regulated launch - audit trails, books and records, and data integrity across on-chain and off-chain systems. Identify accounting, controls, and reporting risks early and ensure each has a clear owner and plan. Required Skills. A degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA, CA, or similar strongly preferred. Strong accounting or finance experience in a regulated setting (capital markets, broker-dealer, exchange, custody, clearing, or digital assets). Experience working directly with a financial regulator - inquiries, exams, or filings. Proven ability to apply accounting rules to new or complex products. Experience building new finance processes for a new product, entity, or regulatory regime. A strong controls mindset and the ability to shape how systems are built before launch. Clear communication skills and comfort in ambiguous, fast-moving environments. Familiarity with the FSRA and its regulatory framework and rulebook. Demonstrates the ability to responsibly use generative AI tools and copilots (e.g., LibreChat, Gemini, Glean) in daily workflows, continuously learn as tools evolve, and apply human‑in‑the‑loop practices to deliver business‑ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in efficiency, cost, and quality. This role delivers sales, administrative, and deposit support while facilitating loan closings and post-closing activities to ensure adherence to internal standards and regulatory requirements.. The Loan Administrator works directly with specialized infrastructure clients, internal partners, legal counsel, and external advisors to solve problems and deliver superior customer service. CLOSINGS - Expedite the closings of specialized industries loans by A) Negotiating loan documents and evaluating alternative structural or documentation solutions, B) Implementing and facilitating the exchange of documents on the closing checklist, C) Confirming the appropriate legal documentation is present and terms match those as approved in the credit presentation, D) Coordinating the deal from checklist through booking, E) Ensuring all closing conditions are met, F) Managing RM/borrower expectations regarding closing timelines through proactive communication and excellent customer service, G) Preparing and reviewing loan closing settlement statements, H) Disbursing loan proceeds in accordance with approved structures and documentation, I) Preparing/Confirming data so loans may be booked properly in the loan system, J) Requesting LaserPro documentation (when applicable), K) Interfacing with borrowers, counsel, agents, internal stakeholders, and customers regarding loan requirements and the necessary preparation for closing, L) Completing accurate loan files, M) Acting as an authorized representative of the company before closing/booking, N) Assessing the appropriateness of waiver requests and documenting approved deviations, O) Negotiating accommodations for approved exceptions, P) Using judgment to determine acceptability of checklist requirements, Q) Reviewing insurance and negotiating changes to meet bank requirements, R) Complete all regulatory requirements for loans (Reg B, Reg C, Reg O, etc).. About the Product team. The Product team listens to our customers' needs and translates those insights into a clear product vision. The team works closely with design, engineering, and analytics to build scalable financial products that empower people to manage their money with confidence. We rely on empathy, curiosity, and business sense to prioritize features and improve experiences. Our role is to lead with clarity, support cross-functional execution, and champion the user in every decision. About the role. The Chief of Staff to the SVP of Product is the strategic thought partner and proxy to the leader. The role exists to scale the product leadership function: by anchoring on the leveraged people problems most central to the org, by owning the external product narrative end-to-end, and by being on point for strategic bets that need a single accountable owner (ex: AI enablement, special projects).. The end goal is a healthy Product org with pillar leads running independently at high quality, decisions made with less latency, and a clearer story about where Product is going, and why. What you'll do. Design and run the product leadership team's rhythms (staff meetings, product reviews, all-teams, offsites): agenda architecture, pre-reads, decision capture, follow-through. Co-own the people rhythms with the HRBP across hiring, calibrations, performance, and talent reviews. Surface emergent structural risks (broken hiring funnels, attrition signals, single points of failure) with proactive solutions. Partners with Technology Operations function to define and improve processes for roadmap planning, driving prioritization decisions, setting annual OKRs and tracking progress to goals throughout the year. . Own headcount planning and budget management alongside the Finance and HR Business Partners: annual planning, quarterly reforecasts, hire-prioritization tradeoffs. Drive AI retooling and enablement, including running internal AI masterclasses for leadership and natively embedding AI-enabled processes across the function. Curate the external product narrative (all-hands, written updates, major external talks): operate as a speechwriter, partnering with PR, comms, and brand. Prepare executive briefings and leadership communications, and reduce decision latency across the Product leadership team. Run a recurring org health pulse (engagement scores, regrettable attrition, leveling drift, manager effectiveness), escalating early signals before they become structural problems. What you'll bring. 10+ years in roles that built product credibility and strategic-narrative chops: strategy with deep product partnership, or a prior CoS role to a senior product or engineering executive at a high-growth tech company. A track record of running people processes at scale (hiring, calibrations, leveling, talent reviews) in a fast-growing organization. Exceptional written communication: you can ghostwrite, synthesize narrative from raw inputs, and draft a board page that holds up under scrutiny. Pattern-matching for organizational dysfunction: the muscle to spot a broken hiring funnel, a single point of failure, or a leadership gap before anyone names it. Comfort operating with influence and without authority across senior leaders in Product, Engineering, Design, Revenue, Finance, and HR. Strong analytical foundation and business acumen: fluent enough in product metrics, financials, and growth analytics to reason about tradeoffs without delegating every quantitative question. Why this role matters. Affirm's next phase of growth depends on Product moving from a function powered by heroics to a function powered by a world-class operating system. title: Lead Product Marketing Manager
description: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter-giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.. As a Lead Product Marketing Manager, you'll play a strategic and hands-on role in shaping how merchants experience Affirm's products. You'll help define our product strategy, lead high-impact go-to-market initiatives, and develop compelling narratives that drive business outcomes. This is a highly cross-functional role that requires strong product intuition, strategic thinking, and a bias for action. You'll bring deep customer and competitive insights to everything you do, and operate as a true partner to Product, Revenue (including Sales, Customer Success and Enablement), Partnership, and Analytics leadership.. What You'll Do:. Shape Product Strategy Through Insights: Partner closely with Product to shape the roadmap by identifying new opportunities, uncovering unmet customer, merchant, and partner needs, and incorporating feedback loops. Leverage customer research, competitive intelligence, and market trends to inform product development and strategic prioritization.. Lead GTM Strategy and Execution: Own the end-to-end strategy and execution of high-impact GTM initiatives across your product area-from beta to full launch. This includes crafting compelling value propositions, developing segmentation strategies, aligning cross-functional stakeholders, and measuring launch success. Additionally, you will analyze complex data sets to uncover insights that inform segmentation, positioning, and refine product marketing strategies. Drive meaningful business impact through scalable programs that accelerate adoption and growth. . Accelerate Product Adoption and Growth: Design and execute programs that drive merchant engagement and adoption at scale. Collaborate with Sales, Customer Success, Enablement, and Partnership to ensure message consistency. Analyze product adoption to inform optimization strategies and identify growth levers. . Enhance Strategic Client Engagement: Develop messaging and materials for key client-facing moments, including bi-annual roadmap meeting with top merchants. Develop product vision and translate into a compelling external narrative that strengthens partnership, builds trust and drives continued engagement. . Operate with Agility and Drive Execution: Navigate ambiguity with confidence and bring clarity to complex, cross-functional projects. Manage multiple high-priority initiatives simultaneously, anticipate risks, and maintain momentum through thoughtful planning and execution.. Affirm is reinventing credit to make it more honest and friendly, giving consumers the flexibility to buy now and pay later without any hidden fees or compounding interest.. On the Underwriting ML team, you'll build and improve machine learning systems that make real-time transaction decisions, assessing the repayment risk and expected value of every Affirm checkout. You'll work closely with experienced ML engineers, platform partners, and cross-functional stakeholders to take models from idea to prototype to production, and to keep them healthy with strong measurement and monitoring as user behavior and macroeconomic conditions evolve.. What you'll do. - You will develop and iterate on underwriting prediction models using a mix of approaches for tabular and sequential data. - You will build and scale feature pipelines and training datasets from proprietary and third-party signals, partnering with data and platform teams when needed. - You will prototype new modeling ideas and features, run offline experiments, and drive the best-performing approaches into production with appropriate risk controls. - You will help productionize models: integrate into batch and/or real-time decision systems, and improve reliability, latency, and operational robustness. - You will instrument and monitor model and data health, and help define retraining/backtesting workflows. - You will collaborate across Engineering, Risk Analytics, Product, and ML Platform to define requirements, evaluate tradeoffs, and communicate results clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.. The Operations Enablement team builds the capabilities required to deliver fast, accurate, and high-quality servicing experiences for Affirm's customers and merchants-while identifying opportunities to eliminate the need for them to contact us in the first place. We partner across Operations, Product, Engineering, Vendor Management, Legal, and Compliance to ensure every agent is trained, equipped, and able to deliver measurable results from day one. Operating across the full servicing lifecycle, we translate new products, policies, and business requirements into scalable operational capabilities. Our work includes designing training and operational readiness strategies, standing up new servicing experiences, defining and measuring interaction quality, and ensuring agents can quickly access the information they need to resolve issues correctly. We use performance insights, customer contact drivers, quality trends, and agent feedback to identify capability gaps and their root causes. We then build the learning programs, quality frameworks, knowledge systems, processes, and tools needed to close those gaps-while helping our Product and Engineering partners address friction upstream rather than requiring agents to absorb it downstream. By owning the full journey-from operationalizing new products and policies to improving existing workflows-Operations Enablement turns complex change into consistent, compliant, and high-quality servicing at scale. One Role, Multiple Teams. We are hiring multiple Manager roles across Affirm's Ops Enablement organization through this single job posting. Rather than interviewing for one specific team, candidates will go through a shared interview process designed to assess the core skills we look for across Ops Enablement. If selected, we will work with you to determine the best team match based on your interests, experience, strengths, and current business needs. You will have the opportunity to learn more about our teams and share your preferences as you move through the process. Potential team placements include:. Customer Enablement: Owning and improving specific customer servicing experiences across multiple product offerings. Horizontal Enablement: Owning programs that touch multiple customer servicing experiences for specific product offerings. About the Role. As an Operations Enablement leader you will help to deliver scalable, compliant, and high-quality servicing experiences across our Operations organization. In this role, you will define and execute strategies that enable our servicing operations to grow efficiently while maintaining exceptional customer and merchant outcomes. You will set the vision for operational readiness, ensuring that people, processes, and enablement systems evolve in lockstep with Affirm's servicing strategy. As a senior member of the Operations Enablement team, you will own a portfolio of cross-functional initiatives aligned to strategic priorities-driving delivery across timelines, dependencies, and measurable business outcomes. You will define and execute servicing strategies by developing clear program roadmaps and execution plans and be responsible for planning, coordination, documentation, change management and measurement across assigned initiatives to ensure operational readiness and measurable outcomes. This role works closely with partners across Product, Engineering, Operations, Compliance, and external vendors to align priorities and ensure readiness for key business and regulatory changes. Serving as a connector between servicing strategy and day-to-day execution, you will translate strategy into scalable operational capabilities. We are looking for a hands-on, data-driven leader who thrives in complex, regulated environments and is passionate about building durable, high-quality servicing experiences at scale. What You'll Do. Own Program Performance: Lead complex cross-functional programs and initiatives, ensuring alignment with servicing strategy, OKRs, and long-term business priorities. Define Program Roadmaps: Develop clear program roadmaps and execution plans, tracking progress against KPIs, timelines, budgets, dependencies, and risks. Partner for Impact: Collaborate closely with senior leaders and cross-functional partners across Product, Engineering, and Operations to align priorities and deliver measurable business outcomes. Drive Stakeholder Engagement: Establish strong stakeholder engagement and governance practices, delivering clear, polished, and executive-ready communications on program status, outcomes, risks, and impact. Manage Risk & Issue Resolution: Proactively identify risks, issues, and dependencies; propose data-backed solutions; and drive resolution in partnership with stakeholders. Lead Operational Excellence: Apply Lean Six Sigma methodologies to identify root causes, implement scalable improvements, and continuously raise the bar for quality, efficiency, and compliance. Own Change End-to-End: Manage the full lifecycle of process and product changes-from design and implementation through change management, adoption, and measurement-ensuring meaningful impact for customers and the business. description: At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter-giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.. About the InfoSec & IT Team. The Application Security team helps Affirm build and launch products that earn customer trust, meet compliance obligations, and reduce business risk. We partner closely with product, engineering, infrastructure, risk, compliance, and other teams to identify security risks early, recommend pragmatic mitigations, and help teams find safe paths to launch. We are looking for an early-career Application Security Engineer who is curious, collaborative, and comfortable working with code. You will help assess application risks, support vulnerability management efforts, partner with engineering teams on secure design decisions, and contribute lightweight tooling, automation, and code-informed analysis that helps AppSec scale across Affirm. This role is a great fit for someone who has hands-on software or security experience, enjoys reading and reasoning about code, is actively developing offensive security skills, and wants to apply those skills in a product-minded, risk-based way. What You'll Do. Partner with product and engineering teams to identify application security risks and help frame them as clear business risks, launch options, and recommended next steps.. Read application code, configuration, pull requests, logs, and documentation to understand how systems work and where security risks may exist.. Contribute small code changes, scripts, detections, tests, secure defaults, or automation that improve AppSec workflows and reduce recurring issues.. Work in GitHub to review code changes, understand engineering context, participate in pull request discussions, track remediation work, and collaborate with engineers.. Communicate security issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, including the risk, tradeoffs, recommended mitigations, and residual risk..
